messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: service=edge-lb-prod severity=P1 — multiple TLS handshake failures & high 5xx rate detected (fired at 2026-03-14T02:22:57Z)

pagerduty-bot: Incident created: PD-18234 — edge-lb-prod / TLS failures + target_unhealthy. Assignment: Alex Chen (on-call).

Alex Chen: acked. I'm on it — pulling healthcheck + ALB target status now.

Alex Chen: digging into logs, initial read: spike of TLS alert 40x failures from healthcheck IPs and client TLS 526s.

Alex Chen: quick check of ALB target groups:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:tg/edge-prod-1
# Most targets: Unhealthy -> Reason: "TLS handshake error: no suitable certificate"
```

Priya Kaur: who rotated certs yesterday in staging-to-prod rollout? I see a cert renewal scheduled at 00:30 UTC.

Dave R.: that was the automated certbot job from ops-kms. It reported success but I saw an alert about SNI mismatch during canary.

Alex Chen: checking certificate presented by the ALB via curl (sni)
```
echo | openssl s_client -connect edge.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername edge.redwood-inference.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -subject -issuer -dates
# subject=CN=internal-edge-2026
# notAfter=2027...
```

Alex Chen: cert CN doesn't match customer-facing host (edge.redwood-inference.com) — looks like the ALB got assigned the internal cert by mistake. That explains TLS handshake failures.

Emily S.: confirmed from loadbalancer config change log: terraform apply by infra-deploy bot at 00:32 replaced listener cert arn with arn:aws:acm:internal-edge-2026.

Carlos M.: that's the wrong ARN — there are two certs with similar names. Quick mitigation: switch ALB listener back to previous cert ARN (arn:aws:acm:prod-edge-2025).

Alex Chen: rolling change to listener now, will do a 1-minute canary on a single AZ.

Alex Chen: applying update:
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elb-listener/lnr-123 --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:prod-edge-2025
```

incident-bot: Modify listener request accepted (change-id: ch-98321).

Priya Kaur: heads up — if we flip cert on the primary ALB, connection resets for in-flight requests expected for a few seconds. Notify support?

Alex Chen: noted. Posting a brief customer-impact blurb in #support right after we flip.

sre-rotation: stepping in to monitor post-change.

(30s later)

Alex Chen: change complete. Verifying.

Alex Chen: re-checking target health and TLS probe:
```
# probe results
TLS handshake OK (edge.redwood-inference.com) -> cert=prod-edge-2025
ALB target health: Healthy=8/8
5xx rate falling from 18% -> 0.5%
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty note: incident transitioned to investigating -> mitigation.

Priya Kaur: good signal. Can we confirm whether any DNS was touched? I saw a separate alert about DNS propagation but that might be unrelated.

Dave R.: no DNS changes in the last 24h in infra audit. That DNS propagation alert looks like a downstream monitoring flake — but we'll keep an eye.

Carlos M.: running a global synthetic check from multiple regions to confirm TLS + LB behavior.

Carlos M.: outputs: EU/US/APAC all show cert CN=prod-edge-2025, handshake OK, 200 on /health. No abnormal latency.

Emily S.: support blurb drafted: "We experienced elevated TLS handshake failures and 5xx errors affecting some API calls. The root cause was a certificate mis-assignment during a recent listener update; this has been reverted and traffic is healthy. We're monitoring. No action required from customers." Shall I post? :thumbsup:

Priya Kaur: post it and include ETA 15m for final monitoring, request support to reopen any escalations from customers.

Alex Chen: posted in #support. Also adding a note in the incident ticket with links to the listener change, terraform run, and cert ARNs.

(10m later)

sre-rotation: monitoring looks stable. 5xx < 0.2%, TLS errors back to baseline. ALB metrics normal.

Priya Kaur: action items for postmortem:
- Lock down cert naming to avoid ambiguous ARNs (infra).
- Add an automated preflight check in CI that verifies listener cert CN matches primary host (devex/infra).
- Improve pager alerts to correlate cert rotations with TLS spikes (sre/reliability).

Dave R.: I'll open infra PR to add a guardrail and tag the correct cert ARN in terraform to prevent auto-selection.

Alex Chen: handing off to Dave for remediation work. I'm off-call in 20m; leave follow-up with the incident ticket.

incident-bot: Incident PD-18234 status: Mitigated -> monitoring.

Alex Chen: closing thread in 30m if no regressions. Thanks everyone. :heart:

Emily S.: filing postmortem doc stub now and assigning owners for action items.

Carlos M.: adding notes about synthetic checks and DNS monitors to catch propagation flakiness separately.

(incident closed later, not included here)
